title: The normalized coefficient reduction square before taking mates
statement: Fix the four small ringed tensor corners S,T,X,Y, exact edges f:S to X, g:S to T, h:X to Y and e:T to Y with isomorphic structural ring maps, a ring-compatible square s and normalized augmented strict coefficient data q [def-sbc-strict-augmented-coefficient-presentation]. For every M in the unbounded derived module category on S, the following maps from towerLeft(h)(towerLeft(f)(rS(M))) to rY(e.left(g.left(M))) agree: towerLeft(h) applied to pf.pull, followed by ph.pull and rY of the ambient derived square, and the exact derived tower square at rS(M), followed by towerLeft(e) applied to pg.pull and pe.pull. The assertion is in the derived category of strict towers, with all transitions; it does not infer equality from evaluations.

proof.text: At a fixed pair of homogeneous degrees, the ordinary square insertion equation says that the two pullback/tensor comparisons send the same pure tensor to the same tensor after the set-sheaf square. The coefficient part is exactly q.square. By module-linearity and the tensor universal property, the degree maps agree. Sum over the total-complex bidegrees: the same signed differential is used on both paths. These equalities commute with every coefficient transition, hence are equality of the actual chain maps of strict diagrams. This is the representative tensor-square calculation underlying the canonical ringed tensor square theorem, now retaining the coefficient sequence.

theorem strictReductionPullbackSquare
    (s : RingedTensorSquare S T X Y g f e h) (q : Coefficients f g h e s)
    (hf : IsIso f.ringMap) (hg : IsIso g.ringMap)
    (hh : IsIso h.ringMap) (he : IsIso e.ringMap) (M : S.mateDerived) :
    (towerLeft h).map (q.pf.pull.hom.app M) ≫
        q.ph.pull.hom.app (f.left.obj M) ≫
        q.atY.r.functor.map (s.derivedComparison.hom.app M) =
      (towerSquare f g h e s).hom.app (q.atS.r.functor.obj M) ≫
        (towerLeft e).map (q.pg.pull.hom.app M) ≫
        q.pe.pull.hom.app (g.left.obj M)
